title: The energy each point would carry
spoken: The energy divided by the effective count equals k B times B times the frequency, which equals h times the frequency.
explanation: Dividing the band's energy among the effective points gives the same amount per point at every volume: k_B B nu, which modern notation writes h nu.
assumptions: Dilute radiation: the density is low enough, relative to temperature, that Wien's law describes the spectrum.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, with A and B for the paper's alpha and beta; they are not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: Energy in the band
notes.explanation: The radiation's energy in the band, the same energy the count was read from.

notes.title: Effective count
notes.explanation: The effective number of independent points from the entropy comparison.

notes.title: Boltzmann's constant
notes.explanation: R over N in the paper's notation.

notes.title: Spectral constant B
notes.explanation: Wien's beta. With k_B it makes an energy per unit frequency.

notes.title: Frequency of the band
notes.explanation: The energy per point is proportional to the frequency.

notes.title: Planck's constant
notes.explanation: The later name for k_B times B, which is R beta over N in the paper.

notes.title: Frequency of the band
notes.explanation: The same frequency, in the modern form of the product.

notes.title: Energy per point
notes.explanation: The step Einstein calls heuristic: radiation of low density behaves, for its entropy, as if it consisted of independent quanta of this size.

notes.title: The same product in modern notation
notes.explanation: Writing k_B B as h renames the constant; it does not add a premise.
